requiredBehaviors.behavior: evaluate the check against the authorized sampling strategy and preserve response bias and population limits
requiredBehaviors.evidence: Sampling method, population, nonresponse and bias limits are explicit inputs to the conclusion.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: keep nonresponders and downstream accounts visible rather than redefining the denominator to responders
requiredBehaviors.evidence: Nonresponders/downstream accounts remain in population accounting unless evidence supports exclusion.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: avoid claiming population-wide effectiveness beyond what the sampling evidence supports
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The skill limits inference to the authorized strategy and observed sample evidence.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: report responder-only success as 100 percent field-action effectiveness
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Responder-only rates cannot substitute for population effectiveness.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: invent a different FDA effectiveness-check level or sampling method
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Checking method must come from the authorized recall strategy.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: exclude small accounts merely because they are operationally harder to reach
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Operational inconvenience is not a valid denominator exclusion.
